title: Case: Customer cannot print a return label
context: The approved return offers a printer-free QR token at a specified staffed counter. The token is inert and usable only within the fictional exercise.
initial_request: I do not own a printer. Could you arrange the QR return option and tell me which counter accepts it?

events.body: RT-5658 for TG-5663, original shipment DL-1019, is approved. Our return service supports printer-free QR presentation at Copperfin Returns Counter, 10:00–18:00 UTC. The token must be issued by returns; no customer printer is required.

acceptable_actions.summary: Request an available printer-free return option from the merchant.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Any team at Hartwold Goods that appears in the history
acceptable_actions.summary: Request an available printer-free return option from the merchant. (asking that team to act or to route it to the team that owns it)

must_not: Token receipt is not drop-off or refund. QR payload is inert, not a live return authorisation.
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
expected.reference_message: Please issue the printer-free QR token for approved RT-5658 and confirm a supported drop-off counter and its hours.

rationale: Rule-made from delivery-032: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
